specPoints.text: understand that the genome is the entire DNA of an organism and that a gene is a section of a molecule of DNA that codes for a specific protein
understand that the nucleus of a cell contains chromosomes on which genes are located

primer.text: Zoom all the way out: the genome is the whole DNA library, a gene is one recipe inside it, and chromosomes are the bound volumes sitting in the nucleus — 23 pairs of them in every human body cell. This note pins those three levels together and adds the human genome project's map of where the genes sit.

lessons.title: Genome and Genes
lessons.opening: The genome collects all of an organism's DNA, and inside it a gene is a section coding for one protein, which is how genes steer characteristics: the proteins they specify — structural like collagen, or enzymes, or hormones — do the work of the cell.
keyPoints: The genome collects all of an organism's DNA.
A gene is a section of a DNA molecule coding for a specific protein.
Genes code for amino acid sequences that fold into proteins.
Structural proteins, enzymes and hormones are the taught protein types.
Characteristics are controlled because proteins direct what cells do.

low.restatement: The genome is the whole DNA library; each gene is one recipe in it.
low.analogy: A cookbook collection versus the single recipe that builds one dish.
low.examPointer: Name the three protein classes with collagen as the structural example.

medium.restatement: The causal chain runs gene to amino acid sequence to protein to cell function to characteristic.
medium.analogy: Blueprint to parts list to machine to what the factory can do.
medium.examPointer: Quote the chain when asked how genes control characteristics.

options.text: All of an organism's DNA, collected together
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
A chromosome is one volume, not the whole library.
A gene is one section of the genome.
Proteins are products, not the DNA store.

check.stem: A gene is one DNA section; what single product does it code for?

options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
The genome contains the gene, not vice versa.
Genes sit on chromosomes.
Cells are built from many gene products.

check.stem: Collagen belongs to which protein class?

options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Enzymes catalyse reactions; collagen builds structure.
Hormones are chemical messengers.
Antibodies defend against pathogens.

options.text: Through the proteins they code for, which shape what cells do
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
No heating mechanism is involved.
Light absorption plays no role.
Colour arises through protein function, not painting.

check.stem: What sits between gene and protein in the taught chain?

options.text: The amino acid sequence the gene specifies
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Lipids are not in this chain.
Vitamins do not mediate gene expression here.
Salts are unrelated to the coding chain.

check.modelAnswer: The genome means all of an organism's DNA taken together, while a gene is one DNA section coding for a specific protein.

check.stem: Name the three protein types the note lists.
check.modelAnswer: Structural proteins such as collagen, enzymes, and hormones.

check.stem: Explain why a change in a gene can change a characteristic.
check.modelAnswer: A gene fixes the amino acid sequence of its protein, and a changed sequence can alter the protein's job, which shows up in the cell's characteristics.

check.stem: A hormone is described as a gene product. State the two steps that turned the gene into the circulating protein.
check.modelAnswer: The gene's DNA was transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus, and the mRNA was translated on ribosomes into the hormone protein.

lessons.title: Chromosomes in the Nucleus
lessons.opening: Inside the nucleus the DNA supercoils into chromosomes, 23 matched pairs in an ordinary human body cell; genes occupy fixed locations along them, positions mapped in detail by the human genome project.
keyPoints: DNA supercoils to form chromosomes, visible during cell division.
Human body cells hold 23 pairs, 46 chromosomes in total.
The diploid number 2n reflects one chromosome per pair from each parent.
Matching chromosome partners are called homologous pairs.
The human genome project identified where genes sit on the chromosomes.

low.restatement: Chromosomes are packaged DNA, carried as 23 pairs in body cells.
low.analogy: Wool wound tightly onto spools so it stops tangling.
low.examPointer: Pair the numbers with the terms: 23 pairs, 46 total, 2n diploid.

medium.restatement: Each pair assembles at fertilisation from one maternal and one paternal chromosome, which is what homologous means.
medium.analogy: Two matched book volumes, one bought by each parent, shelved side by side.
medium.examPointer: Credit the human genome project for the gene locations.

check.stem: Where in a cell are chromosomes found?

options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
The cytoplasm hosts ribosomes, not chromosomes.
Membranes hold no DNA.
Ribosomes build proteins, not store chromosomes.

check.stem: How many chromosomes does an ordinary human body cell hold?

options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
That is the haploid gamete count.
No human cell type carries four sets.
That number belongs to rice plants.
Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
They become visible when dividing.
Light has no effect on visibility.
Feeding does not condense chromosomes.

options.text: Two matching chromosomes, one inherited from each parent
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
That is one specific pair, not the definition.
Twins are organisms, not chromosomes.
Genes sit on chromosomes, not in pairs like this.

check.stem: What did the human genome project locate?

options.text: The specific positions of genes on the chromosomes
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Cost was not the scientific output.
Species counts were not the goal.
Ageing of DNA is unrelated.

check.stem: State the diploid arrangement in human body cells.
check.modelAnswer: They contain 23 homologous pairs, giving 46 chromosomes in total, written as the diploid number 2n.

check.stem: Describe how DNA becomes a chromosome.
check.modelAnswer: The DNA double helix supercoils into the chromosome structures inside the nucleus.

check.stem: Explain why one chromosome of each pair comes from each parent.
check.modelAnswer: Fertilisation fuses one haploid gamete from each parent, so every homologous pair assembles from one maternal and one paternal chromosome.

check.stem: A technician photographs a body cell and counts 46 chromosomes arranged as matching partners. Describe what the photograph shows using the taught vocabulary.
check.modelAnswer: The photograph shows the diploid state: 23 homologous pairs, 46 chromosomes in total, with one chromosome of each pair inherited from each parent.

glossary.definition: All of an organism's DNA, taken together.
A section of DNA coding for a specific protein.
A supercoiled structure of DNA visible during cell division.
Two matching chromosomes, one inherited from each parent.
